(1) PRIOR: iter-5 hr=0.0, lr 1e-3->3e-4 gave rmse=0.00633 (best yet, but still >> baseline 0.00521), ssim=0.941, 197/200. Gentler steps nudged rmse down ~1% -- not near baseline. Iters 1-5 (budget, per-scene fit, capacity, warm-start, lr) all pinned at hr=0. (2) FAILURE MODE: N2I converges toward the over-smoothed FBP-consistent mean; the self-supervision target caps recon RMSE above the sparse-FBP baseline. A known N2I pathology on dense phantoms is that MORE inner steps over-smooth MORE (the denoiser regresses to the low-frequency mean). (3) ONE KNOB: n_iter 200 -> 50 (early-stop; keep lr=3e-4, c=16, warm_start=True -- identical to iter-5 except inner-step count). (4) HYPOTHESIS: stopping the per-image fit early (50 steps) may HALT before the denoiser collapses to the over-smoothed mean, preserving more high-frequency detail from the warm-started init and LOWERING rmse toward baseline. If hr rises, over-smoothing is a late-optimization effect and early-stop is the lever. Per the documented ceiling, more likely the warm-started init is ALREADY over-smoothed so early-stop just freezes a still-blurry recon (hr=0). (5) BUDGET: 50 inner steps/scene is far under the 7.0s per-scene wall, so all 200 scans finish FAST (~3-4s each) -> loop well under 1400s; warm-start ep=3 + fast loop + figure ~= 12-15 min << 30-min wall. (6) Loop continues; iter-7 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: lr up (3e-3), pretrain_epochs up (10), unet_c=8, grad_clip, n_iter mid (100).

rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=30, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.002, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_sr=0.0002, outer_wall_s=900, seed=42, rationale=iter-11 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB: per-scene Adam lr 0.005->0.002 (gentler optimization), on iter-7 CHAMPION base (img_sr=0.0002, img_kernel=7 default, n_iter=30). img_kernel REVERTED to 7 (iter-10 kernel 7->5 gave hr=0.1260 = TIED with iter-7 0.1261 on a clean val_n=200 -> kernel is NEUTRAL; the tight range sigma, not window size, sets edge-preservation). PLATEAU: iters 5,7,10 all cluster at hr~0.126 (img_sr-driven ceiling). Per the documented ceiling, more likely lr just changes convergence speed and the SAME over-smoothed solution is reached (hr=0), since the target itself is the limiter. (5) BUDGET: identical compute profile to iter-2 (warm-start ep=3 + 200*7.0s + figure ~= 26 min < 30-min wall). (6) Loop continues; iter-6 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: lr up (3e-3), n_iter early-stop (50), pretrain_epochs up (10), unet_c=8, grad_clip variation.

HYPOTHESIS: with the range kernel now EDGE-PRESERVING (tight img_sr), a WIDER spatial sigma lets each output pixel average over MORE same-tissue neighbours -> stronger flat-region noise suppression, while the tight range kernel still BLOCKS averaging across fibroglandular edges -> cleaner denoise WITHOUT new blur -> hr climbs above 0.1261. rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=200, val_chunk=5, train_n=400, epochs=20, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=10, tv_step_init=0.001, tv_lambda_init=1.0, tv_share_steps=False, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-12 (breast_ct). EPOCHS probe at the K=10 lambda-winner. Best so far = iter-10 (K=10, lambda_init=1.0, epochs=10) hr=0.1471. Depth FALSIFIED twice: iter-4 (K=50, dead lambda) and iter-11 (K=30, active lambda=1.0) both collapse to FBP -- the useful per-pass TV smoothing is fully delivered by K=10; more passes over-smooth back to FBP-RMSE. So hold K=10 and let the 20 scalars converge FURTHER. ONE KNOB: epochs 10->20 (K=10, lambda_init=1.0, step_init=1e-3, mse, per-iter, lr=5e-3, val_n back to 200). HYPOTHESIS: the lambda schedule was still climbing at epoch 10 in iter-9/10; doubling epochs lets it settle at a better per-iter lambda profile so hr rises above 0.1471. FALSIFIER: if hr saturates ~0.147, 10 epochs already converged the scalars and the ~0.147 plateau is the config-only ceiling for supervised-unrolled-TV on breast (step-collapse caps data-consistency; only TV-denoising of FBP is available). BUDGET: iter-10 K=10 epochs=10 ran ~750s; epochs=20 ~ +train ~ est ~1050s, under 1200s wall (val cost unchanged).

rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=100, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, img_sr=0.0002, outer_wall_s=900, seed=42, rationale=iter-8 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB: per-scene steps n_iter 30->100, on the iter-7 CHAMPION base (img_sr=0.0002, img_n_bf=proj_n_bf=1). CHAMPION = iter-7 hr=0.1261 SSIM0.9606 PSNR39.57 (img_sr 0.0005->0.0002 marginal +0.0004 over iter-5's 0.1257; range-sigma optimum is flat ~2e-4..5e-4). HYPOTHESIS: iter-1/iter-3 showed n_iter did NOT help when img_sr was WIDE (0.02) -- more steps just pulled the over-smoothing BF further toward the blurry 64-view half-target. But now img_sr is TIGHT/edge-preserving, so additional per-scene N2I steps should refine the edge-preserving denoiser toward better noise suppression WITHOUT over-blurring (the tight range kernel structurally cannot cross edges regardless of step count) -> hr climbs above 0.1261. If hr FLAT/DROPS, the edge-preserving BF converges fast (30 steps already enough) and n_iter is saturated -> revert to 30 and move to spatial sigma. FAILURE watched: even edge-preserving, too many steps could still creep the recon toward the noisy half-target mean (mild PSNR drop). BUDGET: n_iter 30->100 ~3.3x inner steps; iter-7 ran 692s at n_iter30 on a fast node but iter-1 n_iter120 was 1200s -> n_iter100 ~1000-1100s; outer_wall_s=900 caps it (may trim a few scenes). ONE knob: n_iter 30->100.

rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=False, pretrain_epochs=3, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=300, grad_clip=1.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.001, optimizer=adam, unet_c=16, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=iter-4 SIX-BOX. So higher denoiser capacity does NOT sharpen -- capacity is NOT the limiter. Iters 1-3 (budget, per-scene fit, capacity) all pinned at hr=0. (2) FAILURE MODE: structural over-smoothing from the poor 128-view FBP self-supervision target, independent of budget or capacity. (3) ONE KNOB: warm_start True -> False (back to c=16). Pure per-image N2I: each val scan is optimized FROM SCRATCH on its own sinogram with NO amortised train-set pre-pass init; n_iter raised to 300 to compensate for losing the warm init (this is the SAME knob -- turning off the amortised init -- expressed as the from-scratch regime it defines; no train split is loaded at all). (4) HYPOTHESIS: removing the amortised warm-start tests whether the pre-pass was pulling every scan toward an over-smoothed mean. If pure per-image N2I clears hr>0, warm-start was the culprit. Per the documented ceiling, more likely each from-scratch fit STILL converges to the same over-smoothed FBP-consistent solution (hr=0), because the ceiling is set by the self-supervision TARGET, not the initialization. (5) BUDGET: no warm-start pre-pass (SAVES ~130s), so the full 1400s outer wall goes to the 200 per-image fits at 7.0s each; c=16 + figure ~= 24 min < 30-min wall. (6) Loop continues; iter-5 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: pretrain_epochs (stronger warm-start), lr up/down, n_iter early-stop, unet_c=8.

BREAKTHROUGH PRIOR: iter-5 (img_sr 0.02->0.0005) hr=0.1257, SSIM0.9605, PSNR39.57, recon_rmse8.61e-4 < baseline9.84e-4 -- the FIRST recon to BEAT the 128-view FBP. Root cause: a TIGHT range sigma makes the image BF EDGE-PRESERVING (smooths flat noise, stops at fibroglandular edges) instead of over-smoothing. Iters 1-4 (wide sr=0.02, depth, n_iter) all floored at hr=0 = confirmed the wide-range BF was the over-smoothing culprit, not the N2I loss per se. HYPOTHESIS: the SAME edge-preserving fix in the PROJECTION domain (proj_sr 0.02->0.0005) suppresses sparse-view streak noise in the sinogram before FBP WITHOUT the view-inconsistency that a strong-but-wide proj filter causes (findings.md: keep proj filtering gentle/soft -- a tight RANGE sigma is soft-edged in intensity, exactly the recommended lever) -> hr climbs above 0.1257. If hr drops vs iter-5, proj-domain edge-preservation induces view inconsistency and the image domain alone is the safe lever. BUDGET: value change only, ~1020s like iter-5. ONE knob: proj_sr 0.02->0.0005.

BUDGET: SSIM term = 1 cheap conv/step vs the dominating projection -> same ~990s as iter-4 << 1080 wall. TRAJECTORY: iter-4 0.8539 (warm-start, BEST) -> iter-5 SSIM-loss @0.15 test., gs_outer_wall_s=1080, gs_amp_init_max=0.05

rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=200, val_chunk=5, train_n=400, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=10, tv_step_init=0.001, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=True, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-6 (breast_ct). SHARED-STEP probe (parametrisation family). iters 1-5: step (1e-2/1e-4/1e-3), depth (K=50), loss (l1) ALL collapse the K independent step[k]->~0 -> recon = FBP init, hr0. NAMED failure: with K INDEPENDENT step/lambda scalars the optimiser can zero out every step to sit on the MSE-optimal FBP fixed point. HYPOTHESIS: tv_share_steps=true collapses the 20 scalars to 2 (ONE step + ONE lambda shared across all K=10 iters). A single shared step cannot be selectively zeroed per-iter; to reduce the supervised loss AT ALL via TV it must commit to one non-zero step that does denoising across all 10 iters -- which may find a net-beneficial smoothing the per-iter version escaped. ONE KNOB: tv_share_steps false->true (step_init=1e-3, lambda_init=1e-3, K=10, mse -- all reverted to the iter-3 base to isolate the sharing knob). FALSIFIER: if the single shared step ALSO -> 0 and hr stays 0, the FBP fixed point is a parametrisation-agnostic MSE attractor -> confirms the structural ceiling (findings 2026-05-23). BUDGET: K=10 mse ~750s like iter-3, <1200s wall.

More likely (per the documented ceiling) the extra capacity just fits the noisy FBP target more faithfully and hr STAYS 0, showing capacity is not the limiter -- the SUPERVISION TARGET is. LOSS-FORMULATION probe. iters 1-4 mapped step (1e-2 diverge, 1e-4/1e-3 collapse-to-FBP) and depth (K=50 also collapses) -- under MSE the optimiser ALWAYS drives step[k]->0 and sits on the FBP init (psnr~36.3=baseline, hr0, loss floor ~0.00624 = FBP's own MSE). NAMED failure: FBP-init is an MSE-optimal attractor -- TV smoothing trades pixel-MSE for perceptual quality, so a pixel-MSE loss has NO incentive to move off FBP. HYPOTHESIS: an L1 loss weights outliers (the sparse-view streak/noise residual in FBP) differently from MSE and is NOT minimised by staying exactly at FBP -- so the optimiser keeps step non-zero and does real streak/noise removal, moving val metrics off the FBP floor and clearing hr>0. ONE KNOB: loss_base mse -> l1 (K=10, step_init=1e-3, lambda_init=1e-3 kept from iter-3; K reverted 50->10 to isolate the loss knob and fit budget). All else identical. FALSIFIER: if L1 also collapses step->0 and hr stays 0, the FBP-init attractor is loss-agnostic on dense-view breast -> the supervised-unrolled-TV skeleton cannot beat FBP here regardless of loss (matches findings 2026-05-23) and I pivot to lambda/architecture knobs. BUDGET: K=10 -> ~750s like iter-3, well under 1200s wall.

rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=200, val_chunk=5, train_n=400, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=50, tv_step_init=0.001, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-4 (breast_ct). DEPTH probe. iter-1/2/3 mapped the step axis: 1e-2 diverges (hr0), 1e-4 and 1e-3 both COLLAPSE the learned step to ~0 so the K=10 recon sits on the FBP init (psnr~36.3=baseline, hr0). NAMED failure: at K=10 the optimiser prefers step->0 because FBP-init already has MSE-optimal psnr 36.3 and 10 TV steps cannot out-denoise it, so staying put minimises the supervised MSE. KEY CONTRAST: the classical (non-learned) tv_iterative sibling BEATS FBP on this exact split (hr 0.16 at 200 iters -> 0.355 at 1000 iters) using the SAME TV iteration but with MANY iterations at fixed non-zero step/lambda -- it does real iterative denoising that K=10 cannot reach. HYPOTHESIS: the limiter is UNROLL DEPTH, not step scale -- with enough steps the TV iteration can denoise the FBP noise below FBP's own MSE, giving the optimiser a reason to KEEP step non-zero. ONE KNOB: tv_K 10 -> 50 (5x depth; step_init=1e-3, lambda_init=1e-3 kept from iter-3). All else identical. EXPECT: step[k] no longer collapses to 0, recon departs FBP with net denoising, val_psnr rises above 36.3 and hr clears 0. FALSIFIER: if step still collapses to 0 and hr stays 0, depth is NOT the limiter and the FBP fixed point is a hard supervised-MSE attractor at any K (matches findings 2026-05-23 verdict) -> iter-5 switches loss (l1) or attacks lambda. BUDGET: iter-3 ran ~750s at K=10; K=50 is 5x the unrolled fwd/bwd in BOTH train and val. Train ~5x, val ~5x -> est ~ (750-load)*~3 + load. Conservatively ~900-1100s; still under the 1200s wall. If it risks the wall iter-5 trims val_n or epochs.

FALSIFIER: if SSIM stays ~0.80 flat (or drops), the basis-coarseness ceiling is confirmed as capacity-insensitive in this budget -- 1024 splats still land far below the FBP floor on PSNR/RMSE (hr=0). Prior findings (1024 G at 10k-40k iters -> hr=0) predict FLAT. val_n=15 HELD CONSTANT (gs_outer_wall_s=1080). TRAJECTORY: iter-1 0.8032 (512G) -> iter-2 0.8048 (512G, +steps flat) -> iter-3 capacity test at 1024G., gs_outer_wall_s=1080

NAMED failure mode: FBP-INIT ZERO-GRADIENT TRAP (findings 2026-05-23) -- since R+ ~= FBP, the data-gradient R^T(R*FBP - g) ~= 0 at init, so the supervised loss's only signal is stay-put; too-small a step lets it sit on FBP, too-large a step diverges. The productive regime is BETWEEN 1e-4 and 1e-2. ONE KNOB: tv_step_init 1e-4 -> 1e-3 (geometric midpoint of the bracket; 10x iter-2, 10x below the iter-1 overshoot). All else IDENTICAL to iter-2 (K=10, train_n=400, epochs=10, bs=1, lambda_init=1e-3, lr=5e-3, val_n=200). HYPOTHESIS: at step=1e-3 the unrolled TV iteration is large enough to move the recon OFF the FBP fixed point and do real denoising work, yet small enough to stay in the stable basin (no divergence), so val_psnr rises ABOVE the FBP floor (>36.3 dB) and hr clears 0. FALSIFIER: if step=1e-3 also diverges (like 1e-2) the stable band is narrow -> iter-4 bisects toward 3e-4; if it again collapses to FBP (step driven to ~0) the FBP fixed point is a strong attractor for the data term at ANY stable step -> iter-4 attacks it via tv_lambda_init UP (stronger TV prior gradient to pull off FBP). BUDGET: iter-2 ran ~750s (<1200s wall); identical compute.

Nearest reference = OLD-split breast N2I-BF which plateaued ~SSIM0.9748 and hr=0 (N2I over-smooths dense breast, docs/findings.md 2026-05-22: split-view FBP noise floor makes MSE-vs-half-view pull toward blur). (2) FAILURE MODE: N/A onboarding; goal = does per-image N2I-BF RUN on the new val=200 split under the HARD 20-min budget and produce finite val metrics + a comparison figure? Expect hr near 0 (structurally bounded on dense 128-view breast per the documented risk). (3) ONE KNOB: N/A baseline (solver near-defaults; only val_n set to the required 200 and n_iter sized for the wall). (4) HYPOTHESIS: per-image N2I-BF trains stably (grad_clip=1.0) and gives val_ssim ~0.95-0.97 but hr~=0 because minimising MSE against the noisy 64-view half-set FBP encourages over-smoothing on the already-clean dense breast FBP. (5) BUDGET: per-image N2I cost = warm(2 ep x 400) + val_n(200) x n_iter(120) inner steps on breast's LIGHT 128-view adjoint (18x fewer angles than Mayo 2304). outer_wall_s=1050 hard internal backstop keeps the per-image loop well under the 1800s sbatch wall; iter-1 measures the true per-scene rate so iters 2-5 can raise n_iter safely. (6) Loop continues; iter-2 dispatched on landing. Levers reserved for iters 2-20: img_n_bf/proj_n_bf (BF DEPTH), img_sx/sy/sr + proj_sx/sy/sr + kernels (BILATERAL params), n_iter + pretrain_epochs + lr (OPTIMIZATION), warm_start on/off, train_n. rationale: tv_iterative_supervised-claude-agentic: val_n=200, val_chunk=5, train_n=400, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.005, tv_K=10, tv_step_init=0.0001, tv_lambda_init=0.001, tv_share_steps=False, tv_eps=1e-06, lambda_neg=1.0, loss_base=mse, grad_clip=1.0, rationale=tv_iterative_supervised iter-2 (breast_ct). DIAGNOSIS of iter-1 (step_init=1e-2): hr=0.0, val_psnr=17.27 dB -- 19 dB WORSE than the LD-FBP baseline (36.32 dB), val_ssim 0.719 vs baseline 0.920. SLURM training log (job 772163) is the smoking gun: loss FROZEN at 0.004813 across ALL 10 epochs and every learned step[k]=0.01 / lambda[k]=0.001 PINNED at init (only step_9 drifted to 0.00937). FAILURE MODE (named): STEP-TOO-LARGE OVERSHOOT -> saturated-gradient training freeze. Mechanism (docs/findings.md 2026-05-23 + Mayo iter-3): the data gradient R^T(R f - g) uses the RAW unnormalized adjoint of the 128-view breast forward op; tv_step_init=0.01 (inherited from the classical sibling's tv_lr) is ~operator-norm too large, so f - 0.01*R^T(...) overshoots into a bad clamped basin at K=1, the clamp/divergence kills the gradient to the 20 log-scalars -> they never move -> recon diverges from FBP regardless of epochs. baseline FBP PSNR=36.32 confirms data/projector are fine; only the unrolled step scale is wrong. ONE KNOB: tv_step_init 1e-2 -> 1e-4 (100x smaller; keeps the unrolled iteration INSIDE the stable basin near FBP where gradients flow to the scalars). Historical breast iter-2 (findings 2026-05-23) used exactly step_init=1e-4 and the recon stayed near FBP (loss dropped, scalars departed init). All else IDENTICAL to iter-1 (K=10, train_n=400, epochs=10, bs=1, lambda_init=1e-3, lr=5e-3, val_n=200, grad_clip=1.0). HYPOTHESIS: at 100x smaller step the training UN-FREEZES -- loss DECREASES across epochs, step[k]/lambda[k] DEPART from init, and val_psnr recovers from 17.3 toward/above the FBP floor (36.3 dB) so hr rises above 0. FALSIFIER: if loss stays flat AND scalars stay pinned, the harness is deeper-broken (then iter-3 attacks init: drop FBP-init / zero-init, or deepen K). BUDGET: iter-1 ran 750s total (<1200s wall); identical compute -> ~750s.

rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=200, grad_clip=1.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.001, optimizer=adam, unet_c=16, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=iter-2 SIX-BOX. (1) PRIOR: iter-1 hr=0.0 (val_rmse 0.00640 > baseline 0.00521 -> recon WORSE than 128-view sparse FBP), val_ssim=0.940, only 197/200 scans reconstructed because the outer_wall=900s cut the loop at per_scene=4.5s. Ceiling holds. (2) FAILURE MODE: N2I over-smooths -> recon RMSE above the sparse-FBP baseline; ALSO the per-scene budget was so tight (4.5s) that inner N2I steps were wall-clipped well below n_iter=200, so each val scan was UNDER-fit. (3) ONE KNOB: outer_wall_s 900 -> 1400 (per_scene 4.5s -> 7.0s). Everything else identical to iter-1. (4) HYPOTHESIS: giving each per-image N2I fit ~55% more wall lets n_iter=200 actually complete on all 200 scans; if the iter-1 hr=0 was partly under-fitting rather than pure over-smoothing, more inner steps should DROP val_rmse toward/below baseline (hr>0). If hr stays 0 even fully-fit, that is stronger evidence the ceiling is STRUCTURAL (the FBP self-supervision target itself caps N2I), which is the documented finding. (5) BUDGET: warm-start ep=3 (~130s) + 200 scans * 7.0s = 1400s + figure ~= 26 min... TOO LONG for 30-min wall. Correction: keep outer_wall=1400 but it is the WHOLE val-loop cap, and warm-start is separate; 130+1400 = 25.5 min + ~1 min figure = ~26.5 min < 30 min wall. Fits. (6) Loop continues; iter-3 self-dispatched on landing. Reserved levers: n_iter, pretrain_epochs, unet_c, lr, warm_start on/off.

rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_supervised-claude-agentic: proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=11, proj_kernel=3, proj_sx=0.01, proj_sy=0.3, proj_sr=0.0005, img_kernel=7, img_sx=0.5, img_sy=0.5, img_sr=0.02, epochs=10, batch_size=1, lr=0.01, optimizer=adam, lambda_neg=1.0, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=400, val_n=200, val_chunk=10, seed=42, rationale=iter-11 dual_domain_bilateral_supervised, re-split Breast-CT val=200. SIX-BOX vs BEST (iter-6 proj_n_bf=1/img_n_bf=7/img_kernel7/lr1e-2 hr=0.2555). (1) PRIOR: proj-domain depth gave NOTHING (iter-10 proj_n_bf=3=0.2555, identical) -> image-domain denoising dominates for breast sparse-view; reverted to proj_n_bf=1. Image BF depth was the biggest lever (1->3 +0.027) but tapered (3->7 +0.0035) UNDER the old 5x5/lr5e-3 regime. (2) Failure mode: the earlier depth taper was measured before the kernel(7) + lr(1e-2) improvements; deeper image stacks may now yield more with the better-conditioned per-filter setup. (3) ONE KNOB: img_n_bf 7 -> 11 (best config otherwise: img_kernel7/lr1e-2/lneg1.0/proj1). (4) HYPOTHESIS: 11 chained image BFs at the improved kernel/lr enlarge effective RF further and lift hr above 0.2555 toward ~0.26; if flat/down, image depth is truly saturated ~7-11 and iter-12 pivots to img_sx/img_sy (spatial sigma init) or a train_n/data lever. (5) BUDGET: 11 cheap 7x7 image BFs -> ~150s, inside 20 min. (6) Loop continues. Artifacts saved.

GOAL: does naf (Neural Attenuation Field, per-scene self-supervised INR -- one coordinate-MLP optimized PER breast slice against its OWN 128-view sinogram, no training set) run on the redone breast_ct staged val split and produce a FINITE val_score + comparison.png + recon_raw.npz WITHIN the HARD 20-min budget, scoring under the frozen calibrated-headroom metric (display 0..0.05, mu>=0 floor, FOV-masked)? BUDGET REASONING (load-bearing): NAF has NO training (train_n=0); the ENTIRE budget is the per-scene fit loop, total = val_n x per_scene. Per the user hint, naf is HEAVY so I use a SMALL val_n=20 (NOT 200) kept CONSTANT across all 20 iters so they are comparable (breast val load is deterministic first-20 of the 200-case val split). 1000s outer wall / 20 scenes = 48 s/scene (naf_per_scene_s=48), inside the 20-min compute budget with figure+IO headroom before the 30-min sbatch kill. breast is 512x512 at 128 views x det; each Adam step = a 512^2 MLP forward + 128-view fan-beam forward-project + backward. 48 s/scene buys HUNDREDS of steps -- a GENUINE NeRF-style per-scene fit, so hr=0 here would be a STRUCTURAL verdict, NOT budget starvation. naf_n_iter=5000 is a HIGH CAP so the PER-SCENE WALL (t_limit in fit_one_scene), NOT the iter count, is the governor. Leaner MLP than default (hidden 192->128, layers 5->4, n_freqs 10->8) for cheaper steps => more steps/scene; naf_lr 5e-3->1e-2 converges faster from the water-mu init in a bounded budget. naf_n_clip=0.05 (sigmoid head out_scale), naf_tv_weight=1e-4 defaults. HYPOTHESIS: NAF is STRUCTURALLY FBP-bounded on dense-view (128-angle) breast-CT -- docs/findings.md 2026-05-23 confirms NAF's sin/cos-posenc coordinate-MLP basis is too coarse for dense soft-tissue at 512^2/128-views and cannot beat the ~0.84 breast LD-FBP baseline (hr=0) even at 5x n_iter. Expect val_ssim that does NOT clear the FBP baseline (hr near 0). This iter ESTABLISHES that datapoint on the redone split under the frozen metric -- a real, valid finding (do NOT reduce val_n further or inflate to make NAF look better; hr=0 plateau documents the ceiling for paper section 5.4).
